# Sudharsan V S

> AI engineer building RAG pipelines and LLM agents, and the evaluations that prove them. Data Engineer at Edvoy in Chennai, India, where he designed a production AI workflow system (RAG over email threads, n8n + Hermes + LangGraph, guardrails) and the initial architecture of an application automation that has made 3,400+ submissions. Three public builds (RAG, an agent, and permission-aware RAG) have public code, 147 automated tests in CI between them, and committed evaluation reports.

This file is a plain-text summary of https://sudharsan2816.github.io/ for AI agents and tools. Every number below is on the site, with a link to where it comes from. A structured version: https://sudharsan2816.github.io/profile.json

## What I build

- RAG pipelines: chunking benchmarks, embeddings, FAISS, reranking, relevance thresholds, citations, follow-up rewriting
- LLM agents and workflows: LangGraph, n8n, Hermes, state machines, human-in-the-loop approval, decision rules
- Evaluation: hit@k, MRR, recall@k, citation precision, faithfulness checks, regression suites in CI, live tests
- Guardrails and AI security: grounding model output in evidence, prompt-injection screening, role-based retrieval, redaction, audit logs, HMAC-verified webhooks
- Production backend for LLM apps: Python, async FastAPI, RabbitMQ, GCP Pub/Sub, idempotency, retries, Docker, AWS, MongoDB
- LLM APIs: Claude API, OpenAI API, NVIDIA NIM, Gemini API, prompt caching, timeouts and fallbacks

## Role

- Data Engineer, Edvoy, Chennai (May 2026 to now; promoted from Junior Data Engineer, Nov 2024 to May 2026; Data Intern, Aug to Oct 2024)

## Production work at Edvoy (internal systems; case studies on the site, no public code)

- [AI Workflow Automation](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/ai-workflow.html): in production since October 2026. A Jira poller starts it, RAG retrieves context from the email thread behind each ticket, and a decision directory and guardrails decide whether the system acts or Slack alerts the responsible person. LangGraph workflows extract requirements from university emails, documents and web pages. Built on n8n and Hermes. He designed the architecture and built the workflow and pipeline; colleagues built some components. No impact figures yet: not measured.
- [Application Automation](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/app-automation.html): designed as Junior Data Engineer; prototype released March 2026; in production since May 2026. A RabbitMQ-based pipeline that submits applications on 70+ university portals. 3,400+ submissions in total since the first release; ~95% of runs succeed (successful / (successful + failed), user-stopped runs excluded); ~5 minutes of bot time per submission vs ~30 by hand. As Junior Data Engineer he designed the initial architecture, built the pipeline and its logic, wrote the university configurations, and split it into three containers. After his promotion he optimised it in production: moved it to AWS (his manager's idea), extended it to take new kinds of data without code changes, and brought a submission to about 5 minutes of bot time. The config-per-portal approach was the platform lead's.
- [Pipelines and Events](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/data-pipelines.html): as Junior Data Engineer, 25+ ETL pipelines that normalise heterogeneous external data into one internal format (MongoDB), and an OTP event service on GCP Pub/Sub with webhooks, acknowledgement, duplicate detection and timeouts.

## Case studies (personal builds, public code)

- [Market Research Copilot](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/copilot.html): document-grounded RAG. Fixed-size chunks beat semantic chunking on 32 labelled questions (complete-hit@3 100% vs 90.6%); a sweep picked 305-word chunks with 38 words of overlap; FAISS fetches 20, a 0.35 relevance floor drops weak matches, an NVIDIA NIM reranker keeps 6. A live test passed 9 of 12; after fixes the retest passed 10 of 10. 96 tests in CI. Code: https://github.com/Sudharsan2816/Projects/tree/main/ai-market-research-copilot
- [AI Code Review Agent](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/review.html): LangGraph pull-request reviewer. Every finding must quote a changed line or it is dropped; the verdict is computed in code; approval is a real branch in the graph; HMAC-SHA256 webhooks; one review per commit. 22 tests in CI. Review quality (precision, recall) is not yet measured. Code: https://github.com/Sudharsan2816/Code_review_agent
- [Permission-Aware RAG](https://sudharsan2816.github.io/rbac.html): access control lives in the retrievers, not the prompt. 6 roles, 11 data permissions, 4 source types; 7 of 7 allow and deny cases pass; 29 tests plus the authorisation eval in CI. Retrieval quality is not measured. Code: https://github.com/Sudharsan2816/Projects/tree/main/enterprise-rag

## Skills, and where they're proven

- Production (Edvoy): RabbitMQ and distributed task orchestration; n8n, Hermes and LangGraph agent workflows; RAG over email threads; Slack and Jira integrations; GCP Pub/Sub, webhooks and event-driven design; ETL pipelines and data normalisation; idempotency, retries and failure recovery; Python and async FastAPI; MongoDB, AWS EC2/S3, Docker
- Personal builds: two-stage retrieval (FAISS + NIM reranking); chunking benchmarks and retrieval evaluation (hit@k, MRR); NVIDIA NIM embeddings, SQLAlchemy; role-filtered retrieval, JWT, audit logs; HMAC webhook verification and human approval gates; GitHub API, Claude and OpenAI APIs
